objective: Make Chris Izworski the clear primary result for his name and build a durable page-one moat of independently controlled, truthful, useful Chris Izworski properties while preserving strong earned authority, one canonical Person entity, and distinct non-branded search ownership.

occupancyTargets.principle: Earn as much branded result coverage as possible through accurate, distinct, useful owned properties, profiles, and independent third-party references.

moatTargets.principle: Page-one ownership is measured by independently controllable origins, not by how many URLs exist under one site or account.

slotCountingRules.definition: A controlled moat slot is one independently controllable root domain or one independently controllable account/profile on a third-party platform. Additional URLs, subdomains, author pages, or project pages on the same root or platform can reinforce the entity but do not create another controlled moat slot.

resultClasses.primaryOwned: chrisizworski.com identity, source, project, and substantive author surfaces; only one controlled moat slot for the root
resultClasses.independentOwned: Distinct useful owned root domains that identify Chris as creator or author; each independent root can earn one controlled moat slot
resultClasses.controlledProfiles: Legitimate professional, publishing, developer, video, identity, and social accounts Chris controls; each platform account can earn one controlled moat slot
resultClasses.supportingOwned: Additional pages or subdomains on an already-counted root or platform; useful for entity reinforcement but not an additional controlled moat slot
resultClasses.earnedThirdParty: Independent news, government, association, conference, podcast, publication, and civic pages substantially about Chris; favorable authority but not controlled
resultClasses.other: Results not attributable to Chris or not useful to the branded entity footprint

rules.entityConsistency: Every active owned property with structured data should identify Chris Izworski as creator/author using the canonical Person entity or an unambiguous link to the primary identity surface.
rules.distinctValue: A property earns branded visibility by being useful and topically distinct; do not create thin pages or duplicate sites merely to increase result count.
rules.reciprocalDiscovery: Active owned properties should link back to the main identity/property network where appropriate, and the central Projects/Works surfaces should discover meaningful active properties.
rules.searchOwnership: Subject intent ownership still controls non-branded page architecture. Multiple distinct surfaces may rank for the branded Chris Izworski query family, but branded reinforcement must not create non-branded cannibalization.
rules.brandedOccupancy: For exact and close-name searches, maximize distinct authoritative Chris Izworski results across the top 10, 20, and 30 while keeping every surface accurate and independently useful.
rules.controlledMoat: Judge page-one ownership by unique independently controlled origins or platform accounts. Same-root pages and subdomains are supporting signals, not extra controlled moat slots.
rules.earnedAuthority: Preserve strong independent government, association, news, publication, and civic results when they corroborate the entity. The objective is not 10/10 self-published results at the expense of credibility.
rules.exactNameConsistency: Use the exact public name Chris Izworski consistently across controlled profiles and pursue corrections when authoritative third-party surfaces contain material misspellings.
rules.primaryIdentityPriority: The chrisizworski.com homepage should remain the strongest candidate for branded position #1 when it is already winning. The /chris-izworski/ identity surface reinforces the canonical Person entity and adds branded authority; do not force it to displace a winning homepage.
rules.launchDiscipline: Do not add a planned property to crawlable central navigation until its owned canonical resolves and its production routes are verified.
rules.measurement: Track exact-name and close-name result occupancy at depths 10, 20, and 30, classify every observed result, coalesce same-root and same-platform controlled URLs for moat accounting, and pair the snapshot with branded Search Console impressions, CTR, and average position. Keep observed data separate from targets and expect locale/device variation.

gardenPlanner.activation: After production verification, add it to central owned-property discovery and begin measuring branded and non-branded search performance. It remains part of the chrisizworski.com root for controlled-moat accounting.
